stories.title: Earnings beats ease worries over record U.S. stock rally
stories.summary: A wave of stronger-than-expected corporate earnings is helping quiet concerns that the recent record run in U.S. stocks has gotten ahead of itself. Investors have been watching for signs the rally was outpacing fundamentals, and the current beat rate is being read as evidence that profit growth is keeping pace with prices, per Investing.com.
stories.whyItMatters: If earnings keep validating the rally, it lowers the risk of a sharp, valuation-driven pullback that would ripple across major indices.
whatToWatch: Remaining big-name earnings reports this season
Whether beat rates hold up as more companies report
Any shift in forward guidance from reporting companies
questions: Is the beat rate broad-based across sectors or concentrated in a few names?
How much of the rally is already priced for continued beats?

stories.whyItMatters: The mixed print underscores the gap between cost control and top-line demand that markets are parsing across smaller biotech names this earnings season.

stories.title: China's factory-gate inflation slows more than expected in July
stories.summary: China's producer prices fell more than economists had forecast in July, according to Investing.com, adding to signs of soft pricing pressure in the world's second-largest economy.
stories.whyItMatters: Weak factory-gate prices point to soft domestic demand and deflationary pressure in China, a factor global markets watch closely for signs of slowing growth and commodity demand.

Any policy response from Beijing to counter deflationary pressure
questions: How much of the slowdown reflects weak domestic demand versus industrial overcapacity?

stories.title: Myspace eyes a comeback as an antidote to social media fatigue
stories.summary: Myspace is reportedly angling for a return, positioning itself as an alternative for users tired of current social media platforms, per CNBC Markets. The report frames the effort as a long shot given the challenge of rebuilding a platform that lost its dominant position years ago.
stories.whyItMatters: A revival attempt is a reminder that social-fatigue sentiment could open space for challengers to incumbent platforms, though the report itself is skeptical of the odds.
whatToWatch: Any concrete relaunch plans or funding details from Myspace
User and investor reaction if a comeback effort advances
questions: Who is backing this effort and what's the business model?
Can a legacy brand realistically compete with entrenched platforms?

stories.title: Germany's trade deficit with China widens as Beijing leans less on European industry
stories.summary: Germany's trade deficit with China has grown, with Investing.com reporting that Beijing is increasingly relying less on European industry, a shift with implications for German exporters.
stories.whyItMatters: A widening deficit signals weakening demand for German industrial goods in China, a key pressure point for Europe's largest economy and its export-heavy sectors.
whatToWatch: Upcoming German trade and industrial production data
Any policy response from Berlin or Brussels on the China trade imbalance
questions: Is this shift structural, as China builds domestic capacity, or cyclical?
